title: GET reads a resource
summary: GET asks for a representation of a resource. It should not be designed as a hidden command to delete or charge something.
introduction: GET asks for a representation of a resource. It should not be designed as a hidden command to delete or charge something. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: GET asks for a representation of a resource. It should not be designed as a hidden command to delete or charge something.

blocks.code:
GET /books/17 HTTP/1.1
Host: practice.test
Accept: application/json
blocks.title: GET reads a resource

blocks.text: The client asks for book 17 and says it can accept JSON. The Accept header describes a preferred response format.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Write a GET request for book 22.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not put private secrets in URLs; URLs can appear in logs.
